source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension - Agricultural Extension Bulletin (ព្រឹត្តិបត្រផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), Vol.01 Issue 01, January 2015 - farmer success story on banana chip processing
text:
The chip-making process documented in the bulletin follows several steps. Ripe banana is first peeled and sliced thin, then the slices are soaked briefly in a solution shown to be tinted pink in the source (likely a lime-water or coloring/flavoring dip, used by some processors to firm the slices and improve appearance before frying) before draining.

The slices are then deep-fried in a large wok, stirred continuously so they cook and color evenly, until golden and crisp. After frying, the chips are drained of excess oil, cooled, and dried further if needed before being packed into plastic bags for sale, either loose by weight or in smaller retail-sized packets. Finished chips are shown displayed in baskets and sealed bags ready for market.
